# Sports Performance Psychology

> An independent educational publication covering the mental side of sport: mental skills training, degree programs, certification, careers, and salary data. Written and evidence-reviewed by Hassam Shabbir. Content is educational only and not professional advice; the author is not a licensed clinician.

## Key facts

- CMPC (Certified Mental Performance Consultant) is administered by the Association for Applied Sport Psychology (AASP). It requires a graduate degree, coursework across 8 knowledge areas, 400 hours of mentored experience, and a certification exam (source: AASP, checked November 2026).
- Sports psychologist pay (United States): ZipRecruiter, October 2026, reports an average of $92,813 per year, a typical range of $66,500 to $117,000, and top earners above $146,000. Payscale reports an average near $75,000. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes no separate data for sport psychologists.
- The author is not a licensed clinician. All content is educational and covers mental performance skills for healthy athletes and performers.
